output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely a cooling failure on floors 6-8. The east chiller broke on 4 August and wasn't fixed until 19 August. Rooms on those floors ran at 26–29°C. Floors 6-8 room comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Their overall score fell from 8.6 to 7.4, then recovered to 8.4 after the repair. Floors 1-5 were essentially flat, with overall 8.6 to 8.5, which is within normal variation. Heat made up 56 of 74 negative comments, all from floors 6-8. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and kiosk metrics are unchanged. The survey method is also unchanged. So I would not serve notice on Orrin or pull the kiosks. The evidence doesn't support either move. The maintenance on both chillers was deferred in April under a budget hold, which is the underlying cause to fix. Next steps: reschedule the preventive maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spare parts, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. A follow-up offer to affected guests is reasonable. Do not drop the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score. That would hide a real failure. The 6% rate rise may have contributed slightly to the value dip on floors 1-5. That dip is within seasonal range, so keep watching it rather than reversing the rise. I'm fairly confident in this and collected no extra evidence, because nothing further was likely to change these actions.
